instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of rice in a pot until the water runs mostly clear. Add 2 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered.
Cut the eggplants into 2-inch pieces. Put 4 cups of water and 1/2 tsp of the salt in a large bowl, stir, and add the eggplant for 10 minutes. Drain well and pat dry.
Meanwhile, slice the shallots thin and mince the garlic. Slice the green onions. Slice the chili thin and set it aside for the table.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add half the eggplant in a single layer and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, turning now and then, until browned on the cut sides. Transfer it to a plate.
Add 2 tbsp oil and cook the rest of the eggplant the same way.
Turn the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp oil and the shallots. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until soft and starting to brown.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Add 1 tbsp of the sugar and stir for 30 seconds, until it melts and turns a deep amber.
Add 3 tbsp soy sauce, the remaining 1 tbsp sugar and 2/3 cup water. Stir, scraping up any bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return the eggplant to the pan and add the pepper. Cover, turn the heat to medium-low and cook for 10 minutes, until the eggplant is soft all the way through.
Uncover and cook for 3 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat the eggplant.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in most of the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice. Put the remaining green onions on top and set the sliced chili on the table.
method_notes: No version of this dish had 20 or more ratings, so the lead is the fallback: the best-read exact dish. Fifteen.net has the only rating (the page's visible 5 from 1 vote). The sources agree on the clay pot method: fry or brown the eggplant first, build a shallot and garlic base, then braise in a salty-sweet sauce. This leaves out the pork, fish sauce and oyster sauce, uses soy sauce and caramelized sugar instead, and moves the chili to the table to keep the base mild. A clay pot is not needed.
